stimuli.title: Deepa, Sana, Meera, Pia, Kiran, Uma, Lata, Riya attend interviews, one per slot, on 7 and 21 March, April, May and June. Slots run in chronological order.
stimuli.body:
Use all the following clues:
• Meera occupies March 7.
• Deepa and Riya attend in consecutive interview slots.
• Exactly 4 interview slots fall between the interviews of Sana and Meera.
• Riya attends in May.
• Exactly 1 interview slot falls between the interviews of Deepa and Pia.
• Uma attends on day 7 of a month.
• Kiran attends in April.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are lockers. Some lockers are notes. All notes are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All files are loans.
II. No lockers is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are lockers. All lockers are notes. No notes is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are notes.
II. Some lockers are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are lockers. All lockers are notes. No notes is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not lockers.
II. No lockers is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No files is a lockers. Some lockers are notes. All notes are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All files are loans.
II. Some loans are lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: T > R = Q > S < P.
Conclusions: I. Q ≤ P   II. P ≤ Q.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Either I or II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. Together the alternatives cover every permissible ordering, so either I or II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: R < S = T < Q = V.
Conclusions: I. S > R   II. S < Q.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. T > Q   II. S ≤ T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. Q < X   II. V < U.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
growth digital credit = ka pa lu
growth savings secure = su pa ze
digital savings banking = ze to lu
credit secure banking = ka to su
growth digital banking = to lu pa
What is the code for “growth”?
questions.explanation: Answer: pa. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: growth = pa, digital = lu, credit = ka, savings = ze, secure = su, banking = to.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 21 km east, turns left and walks 24 km, then turns left and walks 3 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 18 km along the initial direction and 24 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(18² + 24²) = 30 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 72 km south, turns left and walks 168 km, then turns left and walks 2 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 182. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 70 km along the initial direction and 168 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(70² + 168²) = 182 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 35 km north, turns left and walks 30 km, then turns left and walks 19 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 16 km along the initial direction and 30 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(16² + 30²) = 34 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of C. E is the son of C. F is the father of C. How is E related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. F is a parent of C, and E is C’s son. Hence E is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: C is the brother of A. A is the mother of B. E is the father of C and A. How is C related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. C is the brother of B’s mother A. Therefore C is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of D. D is the father of E. B is the son of E. F is the sister of D. How is D related to B?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. D is the father of E, and E is B’s mother. Thus D is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 38 candidates, a candidate is 8th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 28. New front rank = 8+3 = 11. Back rank = 38 − 11 + 1 = 28.

questions.stem: In a queue of 59 candidates, a candidate is 20th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1850. It is marked above cost and sold at a 20% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 2590. Selling price = 1850 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.8 = 2590.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 18 days and B in 27 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 11.33. Use 54 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 54 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 140 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 12 km/h and stream speed is 2 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹30000 for 12 months. B invests ₹120000 for 6 months. Total profit is ₹133200. Find B’s share (₹).
questions.explanation: Answer: 88800. Capital-time ratio = 12 : 24. B’s share = total × 24/(36) = 88800.

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹30000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
questions.explanation: Answer: 300. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 30000 × (10/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 70 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 14. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 14.

questions.stem: The average of 21 numbers is 66. One number, 78, is replaced and the average rises by 8. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 246. Total increases by 21 × 8. New number = 78 + 168.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 7 years, their combined age will be 90 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 57. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 14 = 90; x = 19, so father = 57.
